artists.biography: Pajama Club are a New Zealand outfit formed by husband-and-wife duo of Neil Finn (of Crowded House fame) on guitar, keys, and vocals, and Sharon Finn on bass and vocals. On stage and when recording the duo is expanded with Sean Donnelly (keyboards, guitar and harmonies) and Alana Skyring (drums). It’s always been the element of struggle that makes music human and exciting. Neil and Sharon Finn discovered that for themselves at home late one night in their pajamas, having their first jam, making a racket in the grand tradition of enthusiastic amateurs. For Neil, after a career of writing songs and strumming guitars, it was liberating to be behind a drumkit, no chords or melody to navigate, just keeping time and making it swing. For Sharon, after raising 2 fine boys and coping with Neil it was just 3 notes, pure feel on the bass guitar. It’s no wonder they both listened back to this music and felt like something exciting and fresh had been revealed. For the next few weeks it became a nightly ritual, a few wines and into the music room, pick up instruments and push record. And so inspired, Sharon and Neil were compelled to take it further. They invited respected Auckland songwriter and musician Sean Donnelly to lend a hand. The three of them went to work and steadily those jams became songs, a body of work more diverse and dynamic than any of them had imagined. With the album now complete and due for release mid year the Pajama Club are delighted to be joining Wilco at their Solid Sound festival for their North American debut. More dates will follow. The Pajama Club on stage are: Sharon Finn - bass and vocals Neil Finn - guitar, keys, occasional drums and vocals Sean Donnelly - keyboards, guitar and harmonies Alana Skyring - drums Read more on Last.fm. perplexity.description:
Released in 2011 on Lester Records, Pajama Club is the self-titled debut album by the New Zealand band Pajama Club. The album blends electronic and rock elements, characterized by propulsive basslines, atmospheric synths, and dynamic rhythms. Fronted by Neil Finn and his wife Sharon Finn, the music showcases a playful yet sophisticated approach, merging catchy melodies with experimental textures. Tracks like "Hey Now" and "Too Young" highlight the band’s knack for crafting infectious hooks while maintaining a sense of sonic adventure.

As the band’s first and only full-length release, Pajama Club stands as a unique entry in Neil Finn’s extensive discography, diverging from his work with Crowded House and Split Enz by embracing a more electronic-driven sound. The album received generally positive reviews for its creativity and energy, with critics noting its fresh take on indie rock and electronic fusion. While it did not achieve major commercial success, Pajama Club was praised for its adventurous spirit and the chemistry between its members, securing a niche but appreciative audience.
